what: An official-access audit of the Board of Grievances as a possible second corpus, run BEFORE any acquisition attempt. No document was downloaded, no route was probed beyond a plain GET of published pages, and nothing was circumvented.
why: The first verified Saudi judicial AI deployment is in the Board of Grievances, and the existing corpus cannot see that institution. Adding it would be the only way to make the deployment observable. Whether that is lawful and possible is a question that comes before the science.
prohibitionsObserved: no attempt on /_layouts/ or any SharePoint internal path
no endpoint guessing: only URLs that appeared in official pages or search results were requested
no use of a search-engine cache as a substitute for publisher permission
no bulk enumeration, no sitemap crawling, no session replay
a 403, a 503 or a reset connection is recorded as OUR access failing, never as evidence the source does not exist or does not permit access

routesChecked.method: GET via WebFetch and via curl
routesChecked.result: HTTP 503 via WebFetch; connection reset via curl
routesChecked.note: the crawl policy could not be read from this environment. Because it could not be read, NO crawl was attempted. An unreadable robots.txt is treated as a prohibition, not as permission.
the judicial codices index. Known to exist from official and press material; unreadable from here.
the Supreme Administrative Court principles index.

routesChecked.result: HTTP 503; content known only through a search-engine summary
HTTP 200, title only; the system is behind authentication
routesChecked.note: an authenticated internal judicial system. Not a research route and never to be treated as one.
the national platform lists 'viewing the judicial codices' as a SERVICE. A service that offers viewing and a printed copy on request is not a bulk data route.

routesChecked.route: https://open.data.gov.sa/ dataset search for the Board of Grievances
routesChecked.note: no Board of Grievances dataset was found through search either. If one exists on the national open-data platform it would be the preferred route, because it would carry an explicit licence.
the Bureau of Experts publishes statutes, not judgments. Wrong object type for this design.

routesChecked.route: https://sjp.moj.gov.sa/ (the existing corpus source, as a reachability control)
routesChecked.note: included only to show that the failures above are specific to the Board's hosts and are not a blanket network outage.

verdictDetail: Every Board of Grievances route returns 503 or a reset connection from this environment, including robots.txt. Since the crawl policy itself cannot be read, no crawl is permissible: an unreadable policy is a prohibition. There is no permitted enumerator and none was constructed.

secondIndependentBlocker.what: PUBLICATION COVERAGE ENDS BEFORE THE DEPLOYMENT
secondIndependentBlocker.detail: The most recent Board of Grievances judgment collection reported by official and press sources is the collection of administrative judgments for 1444 AH, announced in 2024 and still being described as the latest issue in July 2025. The verified AI events are the Elm agreement of March 2024 and the deployed knowledge assistant recognised during 2024, i.e. 1445-1446 AH.
secondIndependentBlocker.consequence: Even with unrestricted access, the published Board corpus would contain ZERO post-deployment judgments. A pre/post design is impossible for reasons that have nothing to do with our network, and this blocker would survive any access fix.
secondIndependentBlocker.confidence: the 1444 coverage claim rests on press reporting of official announcements; the Board's own pages could not be read from here to confirm a later collection exists.

whatRemainsUsable: the adoption registry entries themselves, which are chronology and were built from published announcements
the AI-principles policy, whose existence is evidence that AI use is governed institution-wide
nothing else: no judgment text, no case metadata, no counts

permissionRequestOption.status: NOT SENT, and not to be sent without the repository owner
permissionRequestOption.whatItWouldAskFor: a research licence to the Board's published judicial codices for 1443 onward in machine-readable form, or confirmation that the digital-portal viewing service permits automated retrieval for research
permissionRequestOption.whyItWouldStillNotRescueTheDesign: it would supply the pre-period only, unless the Board also publishes collections for 1445 and later. The design needs post-deployment publication to exist at all.

alternativeSourcesConsidered.why: the Virtual Enforcement Court is a real deployment but its output is not published as reasoned judgments, so no reasoning outcome is observable

alternativeSourcesConsidered.source: Ministry of Justice commercial judgments, the existing corpus
alternativeSourcesConsidered.verdict: RETAINED AS AN EXTERNAL COMPARISON SERIES, NOT A CONTROL
alternativeSourcesConsidered.why: different institution, domain, publication policy and code mix. It can carry a side-by-side trend, never a difference-in-differences, until pre-trend comparability is demonstrated

alternativeSourcesConsidered.verdict: WRONG OBJECT TYPE even if accessible
alternativeSourcesConsidered.why: a principle is a curated abstraction of a judgment, selected by the publisher. It is not a judgment, its selection is editorial, and a change in the selection process would masquerade as a change in reasoning

designConsequence: The Board of Grievances corpus is NOT acquired in this session and the event-aligned observational design is NOT opened. The AI deployment study is classified E0_CHRONOLOGY_ONLY. Both blockers are recorded so that a future session can re-test the first one cheaply and can check the second by looking for a 1445 or later collection.
